findings.issue_text: Inverted conditional logic in create.handler.ts:148-153: slug is set only when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, but original code set it only when it was NOT enabled; same inversion for requestedSlug in metadata — accidental semantic change in an unrelated file

EventManager.ts:117-119 accesses mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without a null guard; when evt.destinationCalendar is null or empty, destructuring yields undefined and .integration throws a TypeError, crashing every booking without a destination calendar (old code used evt.destinationCalendar?.integration)

handleNewBooking.ts:~1080 calls evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) which throws a TypeError when destinationCalendar is null (optional chaining doesn't help for null); should be evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]

CalendarService.ts deleteEvent (~314): event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId is only evaluated when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the predicate compares against null/undefined and can never match; calendarId ends up undefined and the delete call fails; fallback should use main host calendar or credential-based lookup

CalendarService.ts updateEvent (~255): same dead-code fallback — find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so selectedCalendar is always undefined in that branch and the update targets an undefined calendarId

packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:153, office365calendar CalendarService.ts:72, and larkcalendar CalendarService.ts:127 still hardcode 'first element of destinationCalendar' instead of selecting the entry matching the passed credentialId; for collective events with multiple hosts on the same integration, host 2's credential will attempt to use host 1's calendar externalId (Office365/Lark 404; BaseCalendarService filter matches zero calendars and silently creates nothing), defeating the multi-destination refactor

EventManager.ts (~345 and ~505): in createAllCalendarEvents and updateAllCalendarEvents, the DB-fetched credential is only constructed when credentialFromDB.app?.slug is truthy; credentials without a related app row leave credential undefined, causing updateEvent(credential, ...) to crash in getCalendar or the destination to be silently skipped

handleCancelBooking.ts:~430: the recurring-event deletion branch now runs once per calendar reference inside the new for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference) loop, so with multiple calendar references the same calendar events get deleted multiple times via duplicate API calls

requestReschedule.handler.ts:237: pre-existing copy-paste bug bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar (both operands identical) was carried over into the new array-wrapping code, so the intended fallback (user's destinationCalendar) still never applies

handleNewBooking.ts:~724: the dynamic-user query no longer selects organization: { select: { slug: true } }; downstream logic relying on user.organization.slug for dynamic collective/org bookings will see undefined and silently change behavior

handleNewBooking.ts:~990: teamDestinationCalendars.push(user.destinationCalendar) depends on destinationCalendar being present in every user-fetch path (userSelect.select, eventType.users, eventType.hosts.user); if any select omits the relation it is silently undefined and collective destination calendars are silently dropped with no error — should be verified/covered by a test

handleNewBooking.ts:~1874: the booking only connects destinationCalendar[0] (main host); other collective hosts' destination calendars are never persisted on the booking record, so downstream flows building evt from booking.destinationCalendar (payment webhooks, reminders, cancel) only ever see the main host's calendar

googlecalendar CalendarService.ts (~150): when no destinationCalendar entry matches credentialId, the event is silently created in 'primary' instead of the intended destination calendar or failing — a behavior regression from the old code that used the destination calendar's externalId, potentially writing bookings into a user's primary calendar unintentionally

CalendarManager.ts:220-268: the new externalId parameter is accepted and echoed back in the result but never used to select the target calendar (each service chooses by credentialId), so the returned externalId can disagree with the calendar the event was actually created in when a credential has multiple destination calendars

webhook.e2e.ts:249: the e2e assertion was merely updated from null to []; there is no test coverage for the new multi-destination-calendar collective paths (multiple _calendar references created, updated, and deleted together), which is the core of this PR and where most of the new logic and bugs live

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts deleteEvent (~314): event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId is only evaluated when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the predicate compares against null/undefined and can never match; calendarId ends up undefined and the delete call fails; fallback should use main host calendar or credential-based lookup

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, deleteEvent now computes `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. The `.find(...)` branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it compares each `cal.externalId` against `undefined`/`null`, which will not match a normal calendar entry. That makes `calendarId` end up undefined, causing the code to fall back to the default ("primary") or otherwise target the wrong calendar rather than the event’s destination calendar. This is a concrete logic bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts updateEvent (~255): same dead-code fallback — find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so selectedCalendar is always undefined in that branch and the update targets an undefined calendarId

packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:153, office365calendar CalendarService.ts:72, and larkcalendar CalendarService.ts:127 still hardcode 'first element of destinationCalendar' instead of selecting the entry matching the passed credentialId; for collective events with multiple hosts on the same integration, host 2's credential will attempt to use host 1's calendar externalId (Office365/Lark 404; BaseCalendarService filter matches zero calendars and silently creates nothing), defeating the multi-destination refactor

adjudication.rationale: Yes. After the refactor, `destinationCalendar` is now an array (`CalendarEventClass.destinationCalendar?: DestinationCalendar[] | null`). `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` iterates over each `destination` and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`, but it passes the same unmodified `event` containing the full `destinationCalendar` array. In Office365 and Lark calendar services, `createEvent` still derives the calendar ID from only the first element (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`), and they do not accept/use `credentialId` to pick the matching destination. Meanwhile `CalendarManager.createEvent` now always calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`, but Office365/Lark ignore that extra arg, so for multiple destinations on the same integration they will all attempt to create the event in the first destination calendar’s `externalId`, which can cause wrong-calendar writes/404s. This is a concrete correctness bug introduced/left by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleCancelBooking.ts:~430: the recurring-event deletion branch now runs once per calendar reference inside the new for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference) loop, so with multiple calendar references the same calendar events get deleted multiple times via duplicate API calls

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In handleCancelBooking.ts the code changed from selecting a single calendar reference (`find`) to iterating all matching references (`filter` + `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`). Inside that loop, when `credentialId` is present and the booking is recurring, it constructs `promises` by iterating **all** `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(type.endsWith("_calendar"))` and for each credential deletes events for `updatedBookings` (using each updated booking’s `_calendar` reference). This deletion work is not scoped to the current `reference` (it doesn’t use `uid`/`externalCalendarId` from the outer `reference`), so if there are multiple `_calendar` references with `credentialId`, the same `Promise.all(promises)` block will run multiple times, causing duplicate delete API calls for the same events/credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: googlecalendar CalendarService.ts (~150): when no destinationCalendar entry matches credentialId, the event is silently created in 'primary' instead of the intended destination calendar or failing — a behavior regression from the old code that used the destination calendar's externalId, potentially writing bookings into a user's primary calendar unintentionally

adjudication.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService.createEvent the calendarId is now chosen by searching calEventRaw.destinationCalendar for an entry whose credentialId matches the passed credentialId. If none matches, selectedCalendar is undefined and the code explicitly falls back to `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`. This means that even when `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar` is non-empty (i.e., a destination calendar was intended), a mismatch/missing credentialId will silently create the event in the user's primary calendar. The previous code used the (single) destinationCalendar.externalId directly when present, so this introduces a verifiable behavior change where mis-association no longer results in an error/404 but instead writes to primary.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarManager.ts:220-268: the new externalId parameter is accepted and echoed back in the result but never used to select the target calendar (each service chooses by credentialId), so the returned externalId can disagree with the calendar the event was actually created in when a credential has multiple destination calendars

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts` adds an `externalId?: string` parameter and returns it in the `EventResult`, but it never uses it when calling the calendar implementation; it always calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`. In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent(calEventRaw, credentialId)`, the target calendar is chosen via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` (i.e., by credentialId, taking the first match), not by the `externalId` passed through `CalendarManager`. Meanwhile `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` loops destinations and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`, so if `event.destinationCalendar` contains multiple entries for the same `credentialId` with different `externalId`s, the created event may go to a different calendar than the `externalId` echoed back in the result.
